title: Why India's Imported Scrap Offers Rose About 2.4% to $360-362 a Tonne: Thin Arrivals and a Semi-Finished Steel Uptick
dek: India's imported scrap offers rose about 2.4% to $360-362 a tonne on thin arrivals and an uptick in semi-finished steel, according to kalkine.co.uk.
summary: kalkine.co.uk reports that offers for imported scrap in India rose about 2.4% to $360-362 a tonne. The headline attributes the rise to thin arrivals and an uptick in semi-finished steel. No further detail is provided.
keyFacts: Drivers cited: thin arrivals and a semi-finished steel uptick
whyItMatters: Higher scrap costs feed directly into the economics of India's electric-arc and induction furnace producers.
implications: Secondary steelmakers could face margin pressure unless semi-finished prices keep pace; traders may watch arrival volumes closely.
